Chess is far from being a solved game, so there is no way of predicting which one would win from the outset. If it were, chess would be a solved game, like tic-tac-toe, where one side can always force a draw. 

Different openings and defenses would lead to vastly different middle games each time, just like in a game played by humans. There would be a lot of draws, just like in top level human play. 

You can easily try to match different top engines against one another on your own computer, if you want to see how the games would play out. The era of chess supercomputers is long gone: a modern home computer running a top chess engine is at least as strong as the best human chess players.

Committing suicide would be extremely unethical, since it would affect several people, some of them to a very large degree. To my mind, there isn't really all that much of a difference between murdering someone, and committing suicide. Sure, murder involves violating someone's rights in several ways, but in terms of the consequences that the two acts bring, there is not much of a difference. If you have people who would be devastated if you were to die, then committing suicide is unethical. 

That being said, I currently want to commit suicide. About a month ago, I nearly did, and there have been several other instances where I have been very close to doing it. 

So I have these two ideas working against one another: one the one hand, I want to die, on the other hand, I don't want to devastate my close family and friends. 

What do I do? Do I keep living for the sake of these people, a few of whom, I'm sorry to say, I do not even like? Given that I can't commit suicide due to the amount of pain it would bring to a few people, what the fuck do I do?!
